To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dietary restriction and daf-2 mutations both reduce protein translation in parallel to the increased presence of structural muscle cell proteins, which is mediated via the activation of DAF-2.
reduced insulin/insulin like growth factor 1 signaling and dietary restriction inhibit protein synthesis but maintain muscle mass in Caenorhabdtitis elegans.

the abundance of ribosomal subunit proteins is reduced in long-lived worms in response to daf-2 mutations and dietary restriction, and that this is accompanied by a general repression of protein synthesis in long-lived worms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the proteome of long-lived worms and reveals a novel role of insulin/insulin growth factor-1 signaling and dietary restriction in the maintenance of muscle cell volume
the proteome of long-lived worms in response to insulin/insulin growth factor-1 and dietary restriction and the underlying molecular mechanisms.
the proteome changes that occur in response to reduced insulin/insulinlike growth factor-1 signaling or diet restriction, and how they relate to the maintenance of muscle mass.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
daf-2 mutants and dietary-restricted worms are long-lived, because they have repressed protein synthesis, increased stress-resistance, and increased proteolytic activity.
daf-2 signaling and dietary restriction are not only lifespan-extending but also healthspan-extending interventions, as they preserve muscle cell volume and prevent muscle atrophy.
insulin/insulin growth factor-1 and dietary restriction both inhibit translation, whereas only insulin/insulin like growth factor-1 signaling preserves muscle cell volume, but not mass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reduced insulin/insulinlike growth factor-1 signaling and dietary restriction extend lifespan by repressing translation in C. elegans.

the insulin-like signaling pathway and dietary restriction both inhibit protein synthesis, but only dietary restriction increases the abundance of proteasome subunits, and only insulin-like signaling increases the abundance of many stress-responsive proteins.
insulin/insulin like growth factor 1 signaling and diet restriction inhibit translation but preserve muscle mass in C. elegans.
The main takeaway from our work is that

reduced insulin/IGF-1 signaling and diet restriction inhibit protein synthesis but preserve protein mass in C. elegans, and that these interventions have different effects on protein abundance, which is not necessarily correlated to transcript levels.
reduced insulin-like signaling and dietary restriction both lead to a reprogramming of protein synthesis and turnover to extend lifespan.

insulin/insulinlike growth factor-1 signaling and dietary restriction inhibit protein translation in C. elegans, which is accompanied by a preservation of structural muscle cell components and an increased abundance of stress and immune defense proteins.
